title: Core DB migrations: article_verifications and seen_keys tables
description:
Add the two verification tables to the core SQLite database.

What: new migration file in crates/core/migrations/

article_verifications:
  article_cid   TEXT    NOT NULL,
  check_type    TEXT    NOT NULL,  -- 'usenet-ipfs-sig' | 'dkim'
  key_id        TEXT,              -- sha256:<hex> of raw pubkey bytes; NULL if key unavailable
  result        TEXT    NOT NULL,  -- 'pass' | 'fail' | 'no-key' | 'dns-error'
  detail        TEXT,              -- 'domain=example.com selector=s1' for DKIM; null for sig
  verified_at   INTEGER NOT NULL
  CREATE INDEX article_verifications_cid ON article_verifications(article_cid)

seen_keys:
  key_id        TEXT    PRIMARY KEY,  -- sha256:<hex>
  key_type      TEXT    NOT NULL,     -- 'dkim-rsa' | 'dkim-ed25519' | 'ed25519'
  key_data      BLOB    NOT NULL,     -- raw SubjectPublicKeyInfo bytes
  cert_der      BLOB,                 -- NULL in v1; reserved for v2 S/MIME X.509 certs
  identity      TEXT,                 -- domain for DKIM; NULL for sig
  first_seen    INTEGER NOT NULL,
  last_seen     INTEGER NOT NULL,
  article_count INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1

Algorithm:
1. Add migration SQL file following existing naming convention in crates/core/migrations/.
2. Run usenet_ipfs_core::migrations::run_migrations() already calls all migrations in order.
3. Verify cargo test -p usenet-ipfs-core passes with new migration applied.

Defensive rules:
- cert_der column must be present and nullable from day one (S/MIME schema reservation).
- Migration must be idempotent (CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS).
